item.title: YouTube Announces AI Agent and New Creator Optimization Tools
item.description:
YouTube Announces AI Agent and New Creator Optimization Tools

At the annual Made on YouTube event, the company announced updates to the suite of AI-powered creator tools it first unveiled in 2025.

⚙️ Key details

YouTube is introducing an AI “agent” designed to optimize a creator’s channel in the background. Its capabilities include:

  • Catalog Monitoring: The tool monitors back catalogs for content that is trending, relevant to the news, or has taken on a new life, offering suggestions for title and thumbnail tweaks.
  • Content Generation: The agent can generate entire titles and thumbnails based on an uploaded video’s content.
  • Creator Feedback: Creators can request feedback from the tool regarding their own thumbnails.
  • Brand Pitching: According to Amjad Hanif, vice president of creator products at YouTube, the tool can create brand pitches by pulling demographic and audience data from a creator’s channel.

🧩 How it works

YouTube is introducing several A/B testing and optimization features to boost watch time:

Feature Function
Dynamic Thumbnails Assigns one of up to three uploaded images to different audience segments.
Video Testing Tests three versions of a video (e.g., different hooks or structures) with small audience segments.

Regarding video testing, Hanif says the system ensures the three versions are not “dramatically different.” Creators can manually select a “winner” version or allow YouTube to do so automatically after seven days.

#YouTube #AIagents #ContentCreation #VideoOptimization

Source: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them

item.title: Internal Documents Reveal Microsoft and OpenAI Concerns Over AI Content Strategy
item.description:
Internal Documents Reveal Microsoft and OpenAI Concerns Over AI Content Strategy

Internal documents and employee statements from Microsoft and OpenAI indicate that the companies’ AI content strategy may be damaging the web and the economic foundations of the data sources used to train their models.

💡 Why it matters

Internal Microsoft documentation describes a “doom loop” where the company’s AI content strategy threatens the “content supply chain” by creating an end-product that threatens its essential suppliers. Key concerns include:

  • Supply Chain Impact: Microsoft admitted that “LLMs are a product that destroys its own supply chain” because they can act as a substitute for the training data they rely on.
  • Web Traffic Decline: OpenAI experts attributed a drop in referral traffic for sites like the Times directly to AI summaries; they speculated search referrals may be down as much as 60 percent.
  • User Behavior: Satya Nadella admitted chatbots have basically replaced search and removed the need to go straight to the source. OpenAI’s Nick Turley stated that once a user gets an answer from a chatbot, there is “no good reason to click” on a source link.

⚙️ Key details

Documents and employees have highlighted several issues regarding data acquisition and model output:

  • Data Scraping: Hecht characterized the harvesting of data for ChatGPT and Copilot as the “largest theft of labor in human history” and claimed Microsoft’s defense makes a “complete mockery of the idea of ‘fair use.’”
  • Content Regurgitation: Employees admitted GPT-4 “memorized a ton of data and therefore will be insanely good at regurgitation.” Examples show ChatGPT outputting long strings of copy from the Times, Mercury News, The Denver Post, LifeHacker, and Eurogamer.
  • Paywalls: An OpenAI representative admitted to being “unaware” of any effort to remove paywalled content from training data.
  • Labor Impact: OpenAI Policy Director Jack Clark stated the company was “creating systems that substitute for the labor of the people that define the ‘culture’ of society.”

🔍 Perspectives

Person/Entity Viewpoint
Hecht Characterized scraping as the “largest theft of labor in human history.”
Alex Haurek (Microsoft) Stated Hecht’s comments reflect an individual perspective and not the company’s views.
Jordan Usdan (Microsoft) Characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial.
Greg Brockman (OpenAI) Described as more interested in the “gazillions” of dollars potentially made through commercial AI.

#Microsoft #OpenAI #LLM #AIEthics #DataScraping

Source: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web

item.title: Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall
item.description:
Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall

AI firm Fountain 0 has released a new film titled Odysseus: The Fall, which is described as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Production: Written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who created all the music and lent his likeness to the title character.
  • Motivation: Koosha stated he adapted the story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.”
  • Studio History: The studio’s only previous work was an AI film called Dreams of Violets that was featured in Tribeca earlier this year.

🚀 Availability

  • Price: Available to rent for $9.99.
  • Platform: Viewable via a web browser.

🔍 Observations

Because current AI models are only capable of generating scenes lasting a few seconds, the film is described as a disjointed collection of moments stitched together. Reported technical and narrative issues include:

  • Visual Inconsistencies: The height of the cyclops changes between shots, oars bend and twist, a sword transforms into a dagger, and waves move in the opposite direction of the wind.
  • Animation Errors: Mouths do not match spoken words (sometimes moving without sound), and one boat in a fleet is seen moving sideways.
  • Audio Issues: AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and the names of Zeus and Odysseus are pronounced incorrectly.
  • Character and Plot: Characters exhibit baffling acting with unexplained pauses and bursts of laughter. The plot structure is disjointed, with Penelope’s suitors not introduced until the movie is nearly over.
  • Visual Style: Hyperreal human characters are contrasted with monsters that look like “shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s.”
  • Anomalies: One scene features an alien carcass roasting over a spit.

#Fountain0 #GenerativeAI #AIFilm #OdysseusTheFall

Source: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
